standard_prerequisites.name: For an element f of a ring, the torsion functor T(-, f) is computed by the Hom and Ext groups from the localization A_f, so its vanishing is equivalent to the vanishing of Hom_A(A_f, M) and Ext^1_A(A_f, M)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 25974-25975 and again at proof lines 26005-26006
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the vanishing condition on the torsion functor into two explicit vanishing statements about maps out of A_f, which are then proved by hand.

standard_prerequisites.name: An I-adically complete module is the inverse limit of its quotients M over I^n, and Hom from A_f into a module annihilated by a power of f vanishes
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the vanishing of Hom_A(A_f, M) for a complete module.

standard_prerequisites.name: The snake lemma identifies the quotients M over f^n M and E over f^n E for an extension of M by A_f, and a short exact sequence of modules in which the outer terms are killed by a power of f splits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 26012-26013 and at proof lines 26005-26007
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the congruence expressing a given element x as a finite combination of the x_n modulo f^n M, which is the surjectivity assertion of part (2).

core_obligations: For part (1), assume M is I-adically complete and reduce to showing Hom_A(A_f, M) = 0 and Ext^1_A(A_f, M) = 0 for every f in I, which is what the torsion vanishing means (proof lines 25973-25975).
Prove Hom_A(A_f, M) = 0 from M = lim M over I^n M and the vanishing of Hom from A_f into modules killed by powers of f (proof lines 25976-25977).

Prove Ext^1_A(A_f, M) = 0 by hand: given an extension of M by A_f, choose lifts e_n of 1 over f^n, set delta_n = f e_{n+1} - e_n and replace e_n by the convergent series e'_n = e_n + delta_n + f delta_{n+1} + ..., which exists by completeness and satisfies f e'_{n+1} = e'_n, so that the extension splits (proof lines 25977-25989).

For part (2), reduce with the algebra result on surjectivity onto the completion to the case I = (f) with T(M, f) = 0, and for a sequence x_n in M build the explicit extension E of M by A_f with the relations x_n - f e_{n+1} + e_n = 0 (proof lines 25992-26004).

Use the splitting of that extension to obtain an element x + e_0 generating a copy of A_f and the displayed chain of congruences, then apply the snake lemma to get x congruent to x_0 + f x_1 + ... + f^{n-1} x_{n-1} modulo f^n M, which is exactly the surjectivity of the completion map (proof lines 26005-26014).
proof_roadmap: For (1) turn the vanishing of the torsion functor into the vanishing of Hom and Ext from A_f and prove them separately, the second by an explicit infinite correction of the chosen lifts (proof lines 25973-25989).
For (2) reduce to one generator and, given a sequence x_n, build the extension of M by A_f whose relations are x_n - f e_{n+1} + e_n = 0 (proof lines 25991-26004).
Split that extension using T(M, f) = 0, read off the displayed congruence and apply the snake lemma to conclude that every element of the limit is hit (proof lines 26005-26014).
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates I-adic completeness of a module to the vanishing of the torsion functors T(M, f) for f in I, and states the converse as surjectivity of the completion map when I is finitely generated (statement lines 25962-25970). Both directions are explicit: for the first, the proof reduces to the vanishing of Hom and Ext from A_f and then splits an arbitrary extension by an infinite series that converges precisely because M is complete, while for the second it builds, from an arbitrary sequence x_n, the extension of M by A_f whose relations are x_n - f e_{n+1} + e_n = 0, splits it using the vanishing assumption and finishes with the snake lemma (proof lines 25973-26014). The construction of the infinite series in part (1) and the construction of the universal extension in part (2) are the two substantive steps.
